name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years on a long-term residence permit, no single absence exceeding 6 months or cumulative absence exceeding 10 months across the 5-year period. Applicant must be 18+, hold health insurance accepted in Montenegro, and pass a Montenegrin language test.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years on a long-term residence permit, then apply, passing the language test.

requirements.blocker_text: Alternatively, 10 years on a permanent residence permit, with the same age, health-insurance, and language-test conditions.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 10 years on a permanent residence permit, then apply, passing the language test.

evidence_required.document: Health insurance policy accepted in Montenegro
Passport copy, birth certificate, medical clearance

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no single absence over 6 months, cumulative absence capped at 10 months across the qualifying period

sources.title: Lawyers Montenegro (private legal-guide site) -- naturalization requirements: 5 years on a long-term residence permit OR 10 years on a permanent residence permit, age 18+, language test, accepted health insurance, absence limits, and mandatory renunciation of prior citizenship within 2 years

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Montenegro). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a private legal-guide site (tier 3); Montenegro's own government portal (gov.me/psc.gov.me) likely hosts the primary naturalization regulation, but it was not located/fetched specifically for this route in this build (only the general temporary-residence categories page was retrieved, cited in me_family_reunification.json and me_student_permit.json). CLOSED CITIZENSHIP-BY-INVESTMENT PROGRAM, DISCLOSED HERE: Montenegro's 2019-2022 Citizenship by Investment scheme (EUR 450,000/250,000 plus a government donation) was discontinued at the end of 2022 under EU pressure -- see me_investor_residence.json's notes for the fuller picture; no separate citizenship_by_investment file was built since the route no longer exists. DUAL CITIZENSHIP: Montenegro generally does not accept it -- naturalization applicants must renounce their prior citizenship within 2 years of naturalizing. Narrow, specifically-named exceptions exist: individuals who acquired citizenship under the now-abolished Citizenship by Investment scheme, individuals who already held dual citizenship as of Montenegro's 2006 independence, and possible future bilateral treaty arrangements with Serbia -- none of these exceptions apply to this standard naturalization route and are disclosed here as context rather than modeled as alternate requirement groups, since none currently constitutes an open, general-purpose route of its own.
